naming_convention.text: slug (model_key like 'claude-fable-5.1-max-text', model field is a lowercased, dash-joined slug derived from the site's modelDisplayName)
naming_convention.agent: display_name (model field is the site's raw display name verbatim, e.g. 'Claude Opus 5 (High)'; model_key is the payload's contenderName field, falling back to the display name when contenderName is absent)

extraction_method: Chrome DevTools MCP, own page (isolatedContext 'lmarena-rescrape-20260915') on https://arena.ai/leaderboard. The RSC-header trick (fetch with {headers:{RSC:'1'}}) was not retried; per the 20260906 meta.json it has 404'd on every route since 2026-09-03. Instead every route was fetched as plain server-rendered HTML with the page's own fetch(url,{cache:'no-store'}). For each response, every self.__next_f.push([...]) call was located with a bracket-depth-aware scan that is string-literal and escape aware, the array literal evaluated via new Function('return '+literal)() to recover the unescaped flight string, and the per-route strings concatenated in document order. The object following the first "leaderboard":{ marker ("snapshot":{ for the agent arena) was then brace-matched (string-literal and escape aware) and JSON.parsed; a missing marker meant a truncated Suspense stream and the whole route was refetched, up to 8 attempts. This run needed only 1 attempt for all 124 routes (no truncation encountered). The full 124-route list was reused verbatim from the 20260906 meta.json's documented category enumeration (text 29, code 12, vision 10, document 1, search 1, text-to-image 8, image-edit 16, image-to-code 1, text-to-video 1, image-to-video 1, video-to-video 1, agent 4 = 85 category routes; text and vision expose both style_control and raw ('-no-style-control' suffix) variants, every other arena a single raw variant, so 85 + 39 = 124 leaderboards) rather than re-running a from-scratch live category discovery; this run therefore could not detect a wholly new category slug outside that known set, only additions/removals of models within the known 124 routes and outright 404s on a known route (none occurred; 124/124 known routes returned 200 and parsed cleanly, so there is no route-level evidence of a removed or renamed arena/category since 20260906). URL exceptions unchanged: image-to-code lives at /leaderboard/code/image-to-webdev (no /overall) and video-to-video at /leaderboard/video-edit. All 124 routes were fetched by 6 concurrent workers inside one fire-and-forget async task held in the page's own JS context (window.__LB), polled from later evaluate_script calls so a slow site could not time an evaluate_script call out; this was necessary this run because a first attempt to return the ~30MB combined result inline (without the filePath option) crashed the chrome-devtools MCP connection entirely and lost the browser session's tabs, forcing a full re-scrape on a fresh page. The second attempt saved the combined result straight to disk via evaluate_script's filePath option, then a local Python script (never the model) split the file into raw.json and normalized.json and computed the row/model diagnostics reported below; no benchmark score was read, retyped, or otherwise passed through the agent's own output at any point. benchmark slugs were taken verbatim from the trailing slug of each payload's own "id" field (leaderboard-sets/public/leaderboards/<slug>/leaderboard-snapshots/latest); the agent arena has no such id field, so its benchmarks keep the 'arena-agent-{category}' naming used since 2026-09-03.
notes: lmarena.ai still redirects to arena.ai. source_url is kept as the requested lmarena.ai URL; every per-record source_url points at the live arena.ai page.
No login, CAPTCHA or Cloudflare interstitial was encountered.

The MCP browser session crashed once mid-run: an evaluate_script call that returned the ~26k-row result object inline (filePath omitted by mistake) closed the chrome-devtools MCP connection and destroyed every open tab, including this agent's page and, as a side effect, whatever state other concurrently-running site-scraping agents had in their own tabs. The scrape was restarted from a fresh page and completed cleanly the second time, this time always using filePath for any call that could return the full result. This is recorded here as a burn: never return a multi-megabyte object from evaluate_script without filePath.

Tool contention (10 agents sharing one browser and one global selected-page pointer) was present before the crash: despite calling select_page immediately before every evaluate_script, on the order of 30 consecutive calls executed on other agents' pages (vals.ai, livebench.ai, benchlm.ai, arcprize.org, tbench.ai, artificialanalysis.ai, epoch.ai, deepswe.datacurve.ai, designarena.ai) before one landed on this agent's own page. Every misfire was caught by an in-script hostname guard that throws before any fetch or write, so no wrong-site data was ever captured, and the guard compared hostname EXACTLY ('arena.ai' / 'www.arena.ai'), never with .includes(), so it correctly rejected www.designarena.ai. After the crash and page recreation, this agent had the browser to itself and the second run completed all 124 routes without a single contention misfire.

Every value in normalized.json is copied verbatim from the site payload, computed only by JavaScript running in the page or by a local Python script reading the saved JSON; no score passed through the agent's own text output. Fields the site returns as null or omits (votes, contextLength, pricePerImage, pricePerSecond, modelUrl, license, cost_usd, ci, date, releaseType) are dropped from the record rather than estimated; the agent arena keeps sessions/observations and a one-sided ci {half_width} from the payload's signalCi field, since the agent payload has no rating interval.

New field vs 20260906: release_type, taken verbatim from the payload's releaseType field where present, was not seen in the ~40 lines of 20260906's normalized.json inspected before this run; it is included here as an additional field per record rather than being dropped, per the instruction to go deeper than the previous run rather than trim to its exact shape. price_per_image and price_per_second are likewise carried through as top-level fields now instead of only being mentioned as sometimes-null in the previous run's notes.

'GPT 6 Astra (Max)' newly appearing in the agent arena is notable: on 20260906 'gpt-6-astra-max' existed only in the code arena's webdev board and was explicitly absent from every other leaderboard including agent; it has since been added to the agent arena's roster. 'Claude Fable 5.1 (Max)' and 'muse-spark-1.3 (xHigh)'-family entries added on 20260906 both persist unchanged into this scrape. (5) Extraction mechanism unchanged from 20260906 in every material respect (flight-chunk parsing required, RSC header still assumed dead rather than retried, same two URL exceptions, same agent payload shape, same 'arena-agent-{category}' naming). Zero of the 124 routes needed a truncation retry this run (all succeeded on attempt 1), versus retries being available up to 8 attempts on 20260906; this is expected day-to-day variance in Suspense streaming, not a method change.
Scores drift daily on this site because it is a live Elo-style arena; score and rank differences between 20260906 and 20260915 for the same model are normal movement, not scrape errors.
